title: Observing Colossal and Tunable Near-field Thermal Radiation with A Highly Sensitive Annular Micro-thermocouple Junction
authors: Ken Araki, Wei Han Won, Liping Wang
abstract: Near-field radiative heat transfer between two objects has been theoretically predicted and experimentally demonstrated to exceed far-field blackbody limit across nanoscale vacuum gap distance enabled by evanescent surface waves coupling, while significant enhancement by more than 100 times usually requires sub-50-nm vacuum gaps around room temperature. This is challenging for parallel-plate configuration with millimeter sample sizes due to intrinsic wafer bow and contaminant particles. Sphere-plate configuration with a microsphere attached to bimaterial cantilevers or micro-thermocouple tips has been used to experimentally demonstrate near-field radiative heat transfer down to 30-nm gaps, but it is much less developed because of the challenges in the sophisticated sensor fabrication, low sensitivity and weak signals. In this work, we overcome these challenges by an annular micro-thermocouple junction fabricated at the end of a glass fiber with straightforward thin-film deposition to achieve high measurement accuracy with large Seebeck coefficient 25 uV/K and thermal resistance 8.7e6 K/W. With a silica microsphere attached underneath the micro-thermocouple junction, we report experimental observation of colossal near-field radiation heat transfer over blackbody limit down to 10-nm gap up to 2600 times with quartz and 900 times with doped silicon. Upon phase transition of VO2 thin film emitter, tunable near-field heat transfer up to 430-fold enhancement is experimentally demonstrated at 15-nm gap with 64% reduction. Experimental data agrees well with rigorous modeling based on fluctuational electrodynamics and Derjaguin approximation, and underlying mechanism is understood by energy transmission calculations. The results will advance the experimental study and fundamental understanding of energy transport at nanoscale gaps.
summary: This work reports on the experimental observation of colossal and tunable near-field radiative heat transfer using a highly sensitive annular micro-thermocouple junction. By achieving measurements down to 10 nm gaps, the authors demonstrated heat transfer enhancements up to 2600 times the blackbody limit. The study confirms theoretical predictions and shows that the heat transfer can be actively tuned by inducing a phase transition in a VO2 thin film emitter.
main_problem: The research aims to observe and quantify colossal and tunable near-field radiative heat transfer, which significantly exceeds the far-field blackbody limit.
main_result: The authors experimentally demonstrated near-field heat transfer enhancement up to 2600 times over the blackbody limit at 10-nm gaps using a novel micro-thermocouple junction, and showed tunability using a VO2 phase transition.
method: The study uses an annular micro-thermocouple junction attached to a glass fiber to measure heat transfer between a silica microsphere and an emitter, varying the gap distance down to 10 nm.
model_or_system: The physical system involves a microsphere separated by a vacuum gap from an emitter (quartz, doped silicon, or VO2 thin film). The measurements are compared against theoretical models derived from fluctuational electrodynamics and the Derjaguin approximation.
key_observables: Near-field heat transfer coefficient (h_nfr), enhancement factor over blackbody limit, and the temperature dependence of the heat flux.
important_parameters: Gap distance (down to 10 nm), high Seebeck coefficient (25 uV/K), and the material phase transition temperature of VO2.
main_assumptions: The temperature of the microsphere is assumed uniform due to the large annular junction area; the analysis relies on established theoretical models for radiative heat transfer.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the design and fabrication of the micro-thermocouple junction, show calibrated Seebeck coefficients and temperature profiles, and plot the measured heat transfer coefficient versus gap distance for different materials and phases.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the challenge of measuring near-field heat transfer, details the novel annular micro-thermocouple setup, presents measurements showing colossal enhancement for various materials (quartz, Si), and finally demonstrates tunable control using the VO2 phase transition, comparing all results to theoretical modeling.
why_interesting: While focused on classical thermal transport, the extreme sensitivity and precise control over energy flux at the nanoscale bridge concepts relevant to quantum thermal conductance and energy transport in mesoscopic systems.
